extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and institutional grant administrators preparing unsolicited/investigator-initiated NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using NIH Parent Announcements to submit unsolicited or investigator-initiated grant applications (R, K, T, F, multi-project, supplements, and post-award actions), including which announcement to use, deadlines, and contacts. Covers activity-code selection and submission timing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Parent Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements are broad funding opportunities that applicants can use to submit investigator-initiated applications for a range of popular programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do not specify any particular area of scientific interest; they simply provide the standard forms and instructions needed to apply. Use these when submitting unsolicited or investigator-initiated applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — no specific scientific topic required
rubrics_metrics.description: These announcements do not specify any particular area of scientific interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may propose any relevant research area consistent with the activity code; the announcement itself does not limit scientific topic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard forms and instructions provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements provide the standard forms and instructions needed to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the forms and instructions referenced in the announcement (e.g., FORMS-F/Forms-I as applicable). Check the specific announcement for which application forms are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement duration and reissuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements are open for up to three years and are typically reissued to ensure continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume perpetual availability; verify current release, open, and expiration dates for each announcement and plan submissions within the active window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard due dates and cycle frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements use standard due dates with three application, review, and award cycles each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the three annual cycles when planning timelines for proposal development and institutional approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applications and associated documents (e.g., reference letters) are due by 5:00 p.m. local time of the applicant organization on the specified due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the applicant organization's local time zone deadline; late submissions are subject to NIH policy on late applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify participating institutes/centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all NIH institutes and centers participate on all parent announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting, make sure the institute or center that may be interested in your research is listed as a participating organization in the funding opportunity. Do not submit expecting participation if it is not listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct opportunity-specific questions to listed agency contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct opportunity-specific questions to the agency contacts listed within the opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the contacts provided in the specific announcement for policy, scientific scope, or administrative questions rather than general inquiries, to get authoritative guidance relevant to that announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate submission schedule eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Research project (R01), exploratory/developmental (R21) and planning grant (R34) applications with a PD/PI appointed to an NIH Peer Review advisory group may be eligible for an alternate submission schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Continuous Submission' for details and review assignment cutoff dates. Confirm eligibility and alternate deadlines before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate activity code and clinical trial designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements are organized by activity code (e.g., R01, R21, R03, R13, T32, K01, F31, etc.) and indicate clinical trial status (Clinical Trial Required, Clinical Trial Not Allowed, Clinical Trial Optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the announcement whose activity code and clinical trial designation match your planned project (for example: 'Parent R01 Clinical Trial Required' vs 'Parent R01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed'). Using the wrong announcement may render the application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe announcement-specific release/open/expiration dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Parent Announcement lists Release Date, Open Date, and Expiration Date (the window during which applications may be submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submission so it occurs between the Open Date and Expiration Date listed for the specific PA/announcement number. Examples on the page show multiple PAs with their corresponding dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know mechanism types covered by parent announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements are available for various mechanisms: Research (R), Multi-Project, Research Training (T), Career Development (K), Fellowships (F), Administrative Supplements, and Post-award Administrative Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which mechanism aligns with your career stage, project scale, or administrative need (e.g., select T32 for institutional training, K awards for career development, F for individual fellowships, PF5 for collaborative international projects, PA-26-001 for admin supplements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements and post-award actions have dedicated parent PAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Supplements to existing NIH grants and cooperative agreements and post-award administrative actions (e.g., Successor-in-Interest, Change of Recipient Organization) are handled via specific Parent Announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate Parent PA numbers (examples provided) and adhere to their specific Open/Expiration dates and any action-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided contacts for technical website issues
rubrics_metrics.description: For technical issues, e-mail OER Webmaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the contact for technical/site problems (not for scientific or programmatic questions); use the announcement-listed contacts for opportunity-specific programmatic questions.
